items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Vocabulary: hobbies: building dollhouses, riding a horse, collecting teddy bears, collecting coins, gardening, making models.
 - Functional language: Talking about hobbies and asking about hobbies (What do you do in your free time? / My hobby is... / Do you like...?).
 Skill focus:
 - Listening.
 - Reading.
 - Speaking.
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Use vocabulary about hobbies to talk about favourite hobbies.
 Skills:
 - Listening: Identify the main ideas in a conversation about hobbies.
 - Reading: Identify specific information in a conversation about hobbies.
 - Speaking: Ask and answer about hobbies using simple questions and answers.
 Value:
 - Appreciate different hobbies and respect others' interests.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Review hobby vocabulary with pictures and word cards.
 - Practise asking and answering “Do you like ...?” with sentence frames.
 Core group:
 - Complete the Getting Started tasks and check answers in pairs.
 - Do a class hobby survey by asking three classmates about their hobbies.
 Challenge group:
 - Report the survey results to the class using simple sentences.
 - Identify the most popular hobby in the class and give one reason why students like it.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during listening and speaking activities.
 - Reading comprehension assessment (True/False, matching, classification).
 - Pair speaking assessment.
 - Write one sentence about your favourite hobby.
 - Class survey worksheet on classmates' hobbies.

items.contents:
Language focus:

 - Vocabulary pattern: verbs of liking and disliking + V-ing, e.g. like/love/enjoy/hate + V-ing
 - Pronunciation: /ə/ and /ɜː/.
 Skill focus:
- Listening
- Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Use vocabulary about hobbies and verbs of liking/disliking to talk about hobbies.
 Skills:
- Listening: Distinguish the sounds /ə/ and /ɜː/ in hobby words and sentences.
- Speaking: Describe hobbies using go, do, collect and verbs of liking or disliking followed by the -ing form.
Value:
- Respect classmates’ different choices of hobbies.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match words with pictures.
 - Complete -ing form exercises.

 Core group:
 - Describe the pictures using verbs of liking/disliking.
 - Complete pronunciation tasks independently.
 - Ask and answer about favourite hobbies.
 Challenge group:
 - Talk about hobbies using different verbs of liking/disliking.
 - Create extra sentences using new vocabulary.
items.assess:
- Teacher observation during vocabulary and speaking activities.
 - Vocabulary assessment (matching and sentence completion).
 - Pronunciation check of /ə/ and /ɜː/.
 - Pair speaking assessment using hobby descriptions.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
 - Topic vocabulary for the Bardout family and their life and work on a boat.

Language Use:

items.activities:
Support group:

items.section: 2.1 Solids, liquids and gases - Properties and classification
items.contents:
Language Focus:
- Key vocabulary: matter, states of matter, properties, volume, compressed and decision.
- Properties of solids, liquids and gases: shape, volume, ability to flow, pour and be compressed.
- Sentence patterns: Matter is either...; One property of a... is that...; A... can/cannot...; ...is a solid/liquid/gas because...
- Singular and plural verb forms in Science sentences.
Skills Focus:
- Reading
- Speaking
- Writing
items.sb:
Resources:
- Open the Teacher Guide first for the teaching flow and materials; use the Student Handout during the lesson.
- Refer to the Teacher Handout for source content and original activities; use the Workbook as indicated in the Teacher Guide.
- Teachers may flexibly adapt the Teacher Guide and Student Handout to suit students while maintaining the learning outcomes and safety requirements.

Week 1_U2.1_Properties
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Name and classify solids, liquids and gases.
- Describe the properties of the three states of matter.
- Explain classification decisions using because and relevant properties.
- Use singular and plural verbs accurately in Science sentences.
Skills:
- Reading: identify key definitions and properties in short Science texts, tables and questions.
- Speaking: classify materials and justify decisions using complete Science sentences.
- Writing: record predictions, observations and properties and answer questions using evidence.
Value:
- Develop accuracy and evidence-based thinking when classifying and describing materials.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Provide a vocabulary bank, pictures and classification sentence frames.
- Allow students to identify an observed property orally before writing.
- Use a partially completed prediction and observation table.
Core group:
- Classify materials and justify each decision independently.
- Complete the demonstration record, Questions 1-7 and Workbook activities.
- Write two complete sentences using the target Science vocabulary.
Challenge group:
- Explain why a hollow sponge or ball can be squashed although the solid material is not normally compressible.
- Discuss how the properties of gases make bicycle tyres more comfortable than solid tyres.
items.assess:
- Classification table and oral justifications.
- Vocabulary matching and guided knowledge notes.
- Prediction, observation and property record.
- Questions 1-7.
- Workbook exercises.
- Science sentence task.
- Exit Ticket.

items.section: 2.1 Solids, liquids and gases - Particle theory
items.contents:
Language Focus:
- Key vocabulary: particle, hypothesis, theory, pour, flow, vibrate and vacuum.
- Development of a scientific theory: observation, hypothesis, investigation and theory.
- Arrangement and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases.
- Particle explanations for fixed shape, fixed volume, flow and compression.
- Language for explaining cause and effect and evaluating strengths and weaknesses.
- Singular and plural forms: hypothesis/hypotheses and theory/theories.
Skills Focus:
- Listening
- Speaking
- Writing
items.sb:
Resources:
- Open the Teacher Guide first for the teaching flow and materials; use the Student Handout during the lesson.
- Refer to the Teacher Handout for source content and original activities; use the Workbook as indicated in the Teacher Guide.
- Teachers may flexibly adapt the Teacher Guide and Student Handout to suit students while maintaining the learning outcomes and safety requirements.

Week 2_U2.1_Particle theory
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases.
- Explain flow, fixed shape, fixed volume and compression using particle theory.
- Describe how a hypothesis can develop into a scientific theory.
- Evaluate a particle model using strengths, weaknesses and evidence.
Skills:
- Listening: follow explanations, demonstrations and instructions for the human particle model.
- Speaking: describe and compare particle arrangements using accurate Science language.
- Writing: complete particle diagrams and write cause-and-effect explanations based on particle theory.
Value:
- Develop cooperation and critical thinking when creating and evaluating scientific models.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Provide particle-model role cards, labelled diagrams and sentence starters.
- Allow pair rehearsal before students write particle explanations.
- Use a word bank for the guided gap-fill tasks.
Core group:
- Draw and describe the particle arrangements of all three states.
- Complete the human particle model, Questions 1-4 and the states-of-matter poster.
- Write two accurate sentences using particle-theory vocabulary.
Challenge group:
- Explain how a sponge can be a solid but can still be compressed.
- Identify and justify one strength and one limitation of particle theory.
- Evaluate how accurately the human model represents particle behaviour.
items.assess:
- Quick-fire retrieval task.
- Particle vocabulary and guided notes.
- Particle arrangement diagrams.
- Human particle model record and self-assessment.
- Questions 1-4.
- States-of-matter poster.
- Workbook exercises.
- Science sentence task.
- Exit Ticket.
